cards.front: Which ocular motor nerve exits from the dorsal brainstem? [___]
cards.context: Trochlear axons cross before dorsal exit. Each nucleus therefore supplies the opposite superior oblique; the peripheral nerve supplies the muscle on its own side.

cards.context: The optic nerve leaves the back of the globe and carries visual information from the retina towards the brain. It is distinct from the smaller motor nerve supplying lateral rectus.

cards.front: Which cranial nerve supplies most of the motor limb of the gag reflex? [___]
cards.context: The vagus activates pharyngeal muscles after the sensory signal arrives through IX. An asymmetric palate response can help localise vagal dysfunction.

reference.title: Cranial Nerve Testing — Anatomy and Physiology; Technique

cards.front: The rotator cuff stabilises the humeral head against the [___].
cards.context: The four rotator-cuff muscles act as dynamic stabilisers of the glenohumeral joint, helping keep the humeral head aligned with the glenoid.

cards.front: The large muscle that abducts the arm after initiation is the [___].
cards.context: The deltoid becomes the principal abductor after the initial part of shoulder abduction, commonly taught as beyond about 15 degrees.

cards.front: Which scapular fossa lies below the scapular spine? [___]
cards.context: Infraspinatus originates here and externally rotates the humerus. The spine separates it from the supraspinous fossa above.

cards.front: The muscle marked A produces [___] of the eye.
cards.context: Lateral rectus pulls the front of the eye away from the nose. Weakness limits looking towards the affected side.

cards.context: The median nerve passes beneath the flexor retinaculum with nine flexor tendons.

cards.front: Which posterior thigh group extends the hip and flexes the knee? [___]
cards.context: Semitendinosus, semimembranosus and the long head of biceps femoris cross both joints. The short head of biceps femoris crosses only the knee.
